title: A task. A keyboard. Proof.
text: Can I Finish tests whether a keyboard user can complete a real task, and keeps the browser evidence.

title: REAL WEBSITE / APPLE.COM
text: Here is a real example on Apple dot com. Find the iPhone VoiceOver setup guide, using only the keyboard.

title: 39 KEY EVENTS / TASK COMPLETED
text: The runner opens VoiceOver, follows the iPhone setup link, and verifies the destination article. This run passed in thirty nine key events.

title: INSPECT THE ACTUAL RUN
text: Every key has a screenshot, a focus record and a timestamp. The report preserves the actual browser recording, and exports a repeatable task contract.

title: CONTROLLED FIXTURE / BEFORE
text: Now a deliberately broken registration form. The control responds to a mouse click, but never receives focus during eighteen Tab presses.

title: SAME CONTRACT / AFTER
text: Replace that div with a native button, and run the identical contract again. The fixed version reaches registration in five key events.

title: ESCAPE / EXIT / CONTINUE
text: A second fixture catches a dialog that ignores Escape. Its fixed version closes, restores focus, and lets the keyboard journey continue.

title: KEEP THE REGRESSION TEST
text: Download an executable keyboard regression test and rerun it after a change. The runner is free and local. This is reproducible task evidence, not an accessibility certification.
